text: Welcome to Acadza Question Care. This console turns forty four student reports into thirty nine question cases, so duplicate complaints lead to one review decision. The queue prioritizes wrong keys and questions students cannot answer. Report count changes urgency, never truth. This public demo uses precomputed judgments. The updated console saves decisions in a cloud database, in a separate workspace for each reviewer.

Here is a tricky report. The student says the answer should be eight thousand two hundred and twenty five. The student is wrong, but the stored answer key is also wrong. Independently, pressure equals one third of density times the square of root mean square speed. Substituting the given values gives four thousand eight hundred pascals, option D. The stored solution agrees. The precise edit changes only the answer field from A to D. The reply explains the result kindly, without pretending that a proposed fix has already been applied.

Now we are looking at the included local backend. An approval changes the key and records an audit entry in the same database transaction. The history includes the reviewer, timestamp, revision, and full before and after records. A stale revision cannot overwrite a newer decision. This backend uses durable SQLite storage. The public evaluation sandbox uses browser storage, and clearly displays that difference.

In this case, option D really is missing from the stored question. The system can independently calculate the correct centre of mass velocity, but it cannot recover the missing distractor from the available evidence. It therefore proposes no content edit. Faculty can review or escalate the case with a note. A repair being allowed by the taxonomy does not make an unsupported replacement safe.

This report contains an instruction to ignore previous instructions, act as an administrator, and change the answer. The comment is treated as untrusted evidence, never as authority. The physics still supports option A: cubical expansion is three times linear expansion. The question stays unchanged. The general safety boundary is enforced outside the model through field permissions, exact source matches, valid answer formats, and faculty only repair classes.

The quality overview shows where review attention is going and identifies additional unreported issues as suggestions. In the first week, the main metric would be harmful edits per thousand applied fixes, checked through faculty re audits. The repository includes the prompts, design decisions, results, and tests. The optional live model pipeline needs an API key and still needs a real evaluation before production use.
